tools.name: codekit-ast-detail
tools.description: [FILE AST DETAIL] Read one or more explicit source files and return plain-text AST structure details. Use it after codekit-ast-tree has helped you choose the exact files that need deeper inspection.

parameters.name: paths
parameters.description: One or more explicit source-file paths separated by newlines (\n). This tool does not accept directories or mixed path sets, and it supports at most 20 files per request.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: Include condensed comment summaries for functions in the structural output (default: false). Separator-style comment banners and metadata-only lines such as params/returns are filtered out, and each summary is compressed to a short single-line note.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. PURPOSE: use codekit-ast-detail only after you already know the exact source files you want to inspect. 2. INPUT SHAPE: pass one or more explicit file paths through `paths`, separated by newlines; directories, recursive scanning, extension filters, ignore toggles, and Markdown export are not supported here. 3. OUTPUT RULE: the tool returns plain Markdown text directly, starting with a detail summary and then one section per file. 4. LIMIT RULE: the request supports at most 20 explicit files and only supported source files are analyzed. 5. LARGE RESULT RULE: when the inline text exceeds the same client-side AST limit used elsewhere in vulcan-codekit, the tool writes the complete content to vulcan.temp_dir/mcp/cache/ and prepends a cache-address notice to the returned text. 6. COMMENT RULE: keep `comment=false` for the default compact view; enable it only when the condensed function-note summary materially helps file-level reading.

tools.name: codekit-rg
tools.description: [TEXT-TO-STRUCTURE BRIDGE] Run ripgrep first, then map matched lines back to the most relevant AST structures. Use this when codekit-ast-detail alone is too broad and you need only the class/function context that directly contains a regex hit.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: Target directory to search recursively. This parameter is required for a fresh search and must point to an existing directory.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Optional file-extension filter, comma-separated (for example lua,rs,ts). You may also pass common language names such as rust or typescript, which are normalized to their corresponding file extensions. When omitted, codekit-rg uses the same built-in source-code default set as codekit-ast-detail and excludes non-core formats such as css/html/json/yaml.

parameters.name: noignore
parameters.description: Disable ignore rules only when set to true. Leave it unset for the normal ignored-by-default search behavior.

parameters.name: rg_pattern
parameters.description: Ripgrep regex used for the first-pass text search. This parameter is required for a fresh search.

parameters.name: show_full_function
parameters.description: Whether to expand the full source of the matched function or method. Default is false. Keep it false for repository-wide analysis or broad feature lookup; enable it for precise file-level analysis when you need the whole function body.

parameters.name: export_md_path
parameters.description: Optional absolute Markdown file path. When provided, codekit-rg exports the full result as a Markdown document to this path and returns only a generated-file notice with the exact path.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. USE THIS AFTER YOU KNOW THE TEXT SIGNAL: codekit-rg is for regex-to-structure narrowing, not for first-pass repository exploration. 2. SEARCH FLOW: it runs rg first and then only scans matched files with codekit-ast-detail internals. 3. DEFAULT LANGUAGE SCOPE: when ext is omitted, codekit-rg uses the same built-in source-code default set as codekit-ast-detail and excludes non-core formats such as css/html/json/yaml. Treat ext as a file-extension filter; if convenient, you may pass common language names such as rust or typescript and they will be normalized to matching extensions. 4. IGNORE RULE: ignored paths stay enabled by default; pass noignore=true only when you intentionally need ignored search targets. 5. OUTPUT RULE: only structures directly related to the matched lines are returned. By default, function or method hits show only the matched lines plus structure context; enable show_full_function only when you need the full function source. 6. USAGE GUIDANCE: keep show_full_function disabled for repository-wide analysis or broad feature lookup; enable it for precise file-level analysis when the exact function body matters. 7. NO PAGINATION CONTRACT: codekit-rg no longer uses cache_id/page style follow-up calls. If the full result is too large for inline MCP delivery, it automatically writes the complete Markdown result to vulcan.temp_dir/mcp/cache/ and returns a compact preview with the exact file path. 8. OPTIONAL EXPORT: when export_md_path is provided, export the full Markdown to that path and return only a generated-file notice with the exact path.

tools.name: codekit-markdown-menu
tools.description: [MARKDOWN DIRECTORY MENU] Scan one or more files/directories for Markdown documents and return only the `#` / `##` / `###` heading menu with line numbers. Use it to triage docs quickly, identify the relevant file after truncation, and then re-run with a narrower path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Target path. Supports a single file/directory, or multiple paths separated by newlines (\n). Directory and file paths may be mixed in one request and duplicate Markdown files are automatically removed.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Whether to recurse into subdirectories when a directory is encountered (default: false). Keep this false for top-level doc triage and enable it only when you need nested Markdown files.

parameters.name: noignore
parameters.description: Disable ignore rules only when set to true. Leave it unset for the normal ignored-by-default documentation scan behavior.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. PURPOSE: use codekit-markdown-menu only for Markdown triage and document navigation; it does not summarize body text. 2. INPUT SHAPE: path supports files, directories, or newline-separated mixed path sets, and duplicate Markdown files are removed automatically. 3. OUTPUT RULE: the tool returns plain Markdown text directly, not a wrapped content table. The header starts with a dedicated scan-summary block, followed by a top-level file menu and per-file `#` / `##` / `###` headings with line numbers only. 4. IGNORE RULE: ignored paths stay enabled by default; pass noignore=true only when you intentionally need ignored documentation trees. 5. SCOPE GUIDANCE: keep recursive=false for a first pass over docs roots, then rerun on a smaller path or enable recursive when the file menu shows where the relevant document lives. 6. NO CACHE / NO EXPORT: this tool does not write cache files, does not use workdir, and does not export Markdown; if the client truncates the response, narrow the path set and call it again.

tools.name: codekit-ast-tree
tools.description: [DIRECTORY AST TREE] Scan exactly one directory recursively and return a compact Markdown tree grouped by subdirectory. Use it for repository-level file picking before detailed AST inspection.

parameters.name: paths
parameters.description: Exactly one directory path. The parameter name remains `paths`, but the value must contain a single non-empty directory path only; multiple directories and file paths are rejected.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Optional file-extension filter, comma-separated (for example rs,ts,tsx). You may also pass common language names such as rust or typescript, which are normalized to their corresponding file extensions. When omitted, codekit-ast-tree uses the built-in source-code default set.

parameters.name: noignore
parameters.description: Disable ignore rules only when set to true. Leave it unset for the normal ignored-by-default tree scan behavior.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. PURPOSE: use codekit-ast-tree for repository-level triage when you want a compact file-picking view before detailed AST inspection. 2. INPUT SHAPE: pass exactly one directory path through the `paths` field; although the parameter name is plural for compatibility, multiple directories and file paths are rejected. 3. SCAN RULE: recursion is always enabled for subdirectories. Use `ext` to narrow the file-extension scope when the default source-language set is too broad. 4. IGNORE RULE: ignored paths stay enabled by default; pass noignore=true only when you intentionally need ignored trees such as target or dist. 5. OUTPUT RULE: the tool returns plain Markdown text directly, starting with an AST summary and then one compact line per file grouped by subdirectory. 6. PARAMETER SCOPE: this tool does not support comment toggles, recursive switches, or Markdown export. 7. LARGE RESULT RULE: when the inline text exceeds the same client-side AST limit used by codekit-ast-detail, the tool writes the complete content to vulcan.temp_dir/mcp/cache/ and prepends a cache-address notice to the returned text. 8. USAGE GUIDANCE: use the returned directory groups to choose the next smaller target set for codekit-ast-detail or codekit-rg.

tools.name: codekit-patch
tools.description: [FUNCTION-LEVEL AST PATCHER] Re-locate a function or method by structural selector and replace the full function source. Use this when line numbers are stale and you need AST-based function replacement instead of raw text patching.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Target file that contains the function to patch. This parameter is required and must point to a regular file.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Flexible structural selector for a function or method, for example with_vmm, McpServer/with_vmm, or impl McpServer/with_vmm. If multiple nodes match, the tool returns more specific candidates instead of patching blindly.

parameters.name: replacement
parameters.description: Replacement source text. It must be the complete function source, starting from the declaration line. Body-only fragments are rejected.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. PATCH FUNCTIONS ONLY: this tool only replaces function or method nodes, never type names or field identifiers. 2. STRICT INPUT RULE: always pass the complete function source starting from the declaration line; do not pass mode and do not pass body-only fragments. Requests that do not follow this rule are rejected. 3. SELECTOR FLOW: pass the loosest selector first; if multiple nodes match, the tool will return more specific structural candidates. 4. SAFETY: patches are written through a temp-file + rollback flow, validated by generic AST re-scan, ast-grep ERROR-node detection, and target identity re-location before the write is accepted.
